title: Transactional Helm upgrade failures triggering KV-schema drift and tenant quorum desync — emergency hotpatch and runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers on Private/VPC (multi-tenant onprem clusters) reported repeated operator reconcile failures during a staged Helm release. Failures cause partial CRD projection and KV cache divergence leading to tenant quorum desync: control-plane reports succeeded while nodeagents report schema mismatch and subsequent reconciliation removes hooks unexpectedly. Immediate customer impact: degraded inference serving for affected tenants, failed canary rollouts, and one escalated enterprise customer triggering an SLA review. This ticket tracks investigation, hotpatch, customer communication, and long-term mitigation work.
steps_taken: 2026-03-09 02:13 UTC - Pager alert triggered: reconcile_error spikes across three tenant clusters (INC-2026-03-09-PLAT-4721)
2026-03-09 02:28 UTC - Scoped to onprem operator helm upgrade path; reproduced on internal staging with a synthetic tenant upgrade that included an ordered Helm hook set and a CRD migration step
2026-03-09 04:10 UTC - Identified race between helm post-upgrade hooks and operator manifest reapply; operator attempted delta projection while helm finalizer still mutating annotations

2026-03-10 09:45 UTC - Implemented temporary mitigation: operator now suppresses automatic garbage-collection for CRs with helm finalizer present (safe-mode flag), preventing immediate deletion of hook-attached resources
2026-03-11 16:00 UTC - Built and smoke-tested hotpatch operator image with serialized helm-hook-wait logic and added extra preflight checksum verification for tenant-level KV schema
2026-03-12 01:20 UTC - Deployed hotpatch to two impacted customers via controlled canary; observed KV-schema drift rate drop to zero and reconcile error rate return to baseline
2026-03-12 11:30 UTC - Notified customers with summary, temporary mitigation steps, and ETA for full fix; opened PRs for permanent fixes and a recovery subroutine to repair affected tenant KV state
resolution_summary: Hotpatch (private-operator-2026.03.15-hotfix-1) introduces a helm-finalizer-aware reconciliation path and a transactional preflight checksum that prevents operator from projecting partial CRD changes while helm is still mutating resources. Canary deployments to two customers validated the approach; full rollout scheduled with rolling quorum-safe gating. Post-deploy runbook added to automatically detect and repair tenant KV divergence using snapshot restore and transactional reapply. Customer-facing SLA remediation offers 5% credit for affected billing period (sales and legal coordinated).
postmortem_actions: Add gating: operator must detect helm finalizers and wait for helm completion or explicitly acquire helm lock before mutating CRs
Introduce transactional ledger for CRD migration steps to enable replay and idempotent migration
Enhance telemetry: emit tenant-level kv_schema_version and reconcile_timestamps to central dashboard
Create a pre-upgrade dry-run tool for customers that verifies helm hook order and finalizer presence
Document onprem upgrade best practices and embed into Console release notes
open_questions: Should we require a Helm 3.12+ minimum for operator-managed upgrades to rely on improved hook sequencing?
Is it acceptable to keep the safe-mode suppression of GC for 30 days post-upgrade, or should we automate finalizer resolution earlier?
Do we need to backport fix to prior private-operator branches used by customers on LTS contracts?
communication_log: 2026-03-09 05:00 UTC - Initial incident notification to SRE and Solutions Engineering via #onprem-incident Slack
2026-03-10 12:00 UTC - Customer A (Acme Analytics) on-call call: explained mitigation, promised hotpatch ETA 48 hours
2026-03-12 13:00 UTC - Post-canary update sent to affected customers with remediation steps and timeline
2026-03-15 09:00 UTC - Drafted release notes and customer FAQ for hotfix rollout
risks_and_tradeoffs: Safe-mode GC suppression reduces blast radius of in-progress helm upgrades but increases amount of stale resources until finalizer resolution; performing aggressive automatic resolution risks deleting customer resources incorrectly. We chose conservative approach to prioritize customer data safety and SLA stability. Backporting increases testing surface and release coordination overhead but required for some enterprise LTS customers.
